White Midwestern man (30–49), separated, some college, full-time employed with mid income; politically independent but very liberal, lightly religious. Retired white woman (65+, Southern US) with an associate’s degree, low income, living with a partner; Protestant but seldom attends, politically independent/moderate. A very liberal, agnostic, self-employed woman in her 30s–40s in the Northeast who is highly curious, intellectually engaged, and knowledge-rich, with strong verbal/logic ability and high financial literacy. Widowed Midwestern woman (30–49) living alone, some college, working part-time on a modest income; politically moderate/independent and nonreligious. Midwestern white woman in her 50s–60s, divorced and living alone, college-educated, retired with low income; culturally Catholic but non-practicing, politically independent and moderate. White, liberal/Democrat male (30–49) in the US South, postgraduate-educated, full-time employed ($75–100k), living alone and separated; nonreligious. Asian American male (30–49) in the Western US; college-educated, liberal/Democrat, Buddhist with low religious attendance; never married, household of four, currently unemployed with prior mid-to-upper income. White Jewish woman in her 50s–early 60s in the Western US, married in a 3-person household, highly educated (postgraduate), high-income background but currently unemployed; very liberal Democrat with strong pro-environment values and low religious attendance. White Midwestern male in his 20s, never married, Protestant (attends occasionally), very liberal Democrat; student in a larger household with high household income. White male in his 30s–40s living in the US South, self-employed, high-school educated, middle income, living with a partner; agnostic, nonreligious in practice, and politically liberal/Democrat. Married white Catholic woman in her 50s–60s in the Western US with postgraduate education, working part-time and living in a three-person household; politically conservative/Republican and values family stability, being a good parent/grandparent, and building generational wealth. Married white Catholic woman in her 30s–40s living in the US South, working part-time and raising a larger household on an upper-middle income. Midwestern married white woman (30–49) with an associate’s degree, high household income, and a homemaker role in a larger household; conservative/Republican and lightly religiously observant. Married Black man in his 30s–40s living in the Western US; college educated, Protestant (weekly churchgoer), very conservative Republican, high household income but currently unemployed and supporting a large household. Midwestern Black married man in his 30s–40s, high‑school educated, working full time with moderate, independent politics and no religious involvement. Divorced white woman in her 30s–40s living in the Northeast, self-employed with low income and an associate’s degree; politically liberal/Democrat and nonreligious. Widowed white woman in her 50s–60s in the Western US, living alone, low income but employed full-time; atheist and liberal/Democrat. Young white Midwestern man (18–29), atheist and liberal/Democrat, high-school educated, currently unemployed in a 4-person household with relatively high stated income. Married white male in his 30s–40s living in the Pacific region, self-employed with an associate’s degree and mid income; politically conservative/Republican and nonreligious. Young white married woman in the Western US, self-employed with some college and mid income; agnostic, nonreligious in practice, independent but very liberal and strongly pro-environment. Married, high-income, postgraduate-educated white male in the US South (30–49), atheist and very liberal/Democrat, working full-time in a household of four. Hispanic married woman in her 50s–60s living in the U.S. South; high‑school educated, Catholic but seldom attends, moderate Democrat, high household income, works part-time in a four-person household. Black married woman (30–49) in the US South, college-educated, very liberal Democrat, Protestant but rarely attends, household of three, currently a homemaker with mid–upper-middle income. Decision-making tends to be certainty-seeking and optimization-focused (wants the “best” choice, dislikes ambiguity), but he’s not inclined to enjoy complex analysis and has weaker numeracy/financial knowledge, so he may rely on clear rules, trusted heuristics, and concrete guidance. Emotionally prone to anxiety and especially depressive symptoms, with low clarity about identity, which can amplify worry and rumination. Financially cautious and risk-averse, reluctant to spend, impatient for near-term rewards, and tends to mentally earmark money; in bargaining he offers fairness but is skeptical and untrusting, often prioritizing self-protection and reciprocity over generosity.

Middle-aged Black man in the U.S. South, living alone and working full-time on a modest income; socially reserved and low on novelty-seeking, preferring familiar routines and practical, no-frills choices. Extremely conscientious, organized, and reliable, with very low anxiety/depressive tendency and a clear, stable sense of identity; tends to want closure and make deliberate, “best-choice” decisions rather than winging it. Not especially expressive or emotionally empathetic, but strongly fairness-minded and considerate in resource-splitting, while also careful not to disadvantage himself; generally cautious about trusting others with money and expects balance/reciprocity. Thinks clearly under pressure and can override gut impulses, with solid numeracy/financial basics; may dislike long, abstract intellectual deep-dives but handles concrete problem-solving well. Values independence and self-reliance and is politically moderate/independent with low environmentalist orientation; personally recognizes a pattern of overextending for others and is trying to prioritize his own time, boundaries, and happiness.

Married, high-income white woman in her 30s–40s living in the U.S. South; college educated, full-time employed, agnostic, socially liberal/Democrat, in a household of 5+. Quiet, reserved, and low on novelty-seeking; prefers familiar routines and clear rules, with a strong desire for certainty and quick closure when things are ambiguous. Interpersonally she is generally kind, honest, fairness-oriented, and moderately empathic; she tends to share resources and reciprocate trust, while being relatively unconcerned with impression-management. She aspires to be more organized, confident, and goal-directed but currently struggles with disorganization and follow-through, and is prone to worry and low mood. Cognitively she can think analytically and handle numbers well when prompted, but doesn’t naturally enjoy effortful deliberation; she may still overestimate her performance. Financially she budgets in distinct “mental accounts,” can be impulsive with spending, and has weaker general financial literacy; she is not especially minimalist or environmentally driven. Values emphasize personal autonomy with egalitarian instincts more than group loyalty or hierarchy, and she tends to act from principles like equity, honesty, accountability, and integrity.

White male in his 50s–60s living in the US South, single and living alone, agnostic, liberal/Democrat, unemployed with low income and an associate’s degree. Intellectually sharp and highly analytical (strong logic, numeracy, and financial knowledge), tends to think things through and optimize rather than “good enough,” and can be very thorough once he gets started. However, he struggles with low conscientiousness in day-to-day life—low energy, procrastination, difficulty initiating tasks, and time-wasting—along with some depressive/anxious tendencies and only moderate clarity about who he is. Socially he’s about average in outgoingness, somewhat blunt/less accommodating, and not very image-managed, but he values fairness and mutual benefit: generally trusting and generous in cooperative situations, willing to split resources fairly, and aims to be honest while building more patience for differing views. Financially he’s a tightwad who dislikes spending, shows moderate impatience and some present-bias, is not especially loss-averse, and is moderately open to new ideas without being strongly minimalist or uniqueness-seeking; he has average environmental concern and empathy, with a self-improvement focus on fitness, responsiveness to others, and follow-through.

Midwestern white woman in her 50s–early 60s, married, Protestant but non-attending, moderately conservative/Republican, high-school educated, working full-time with mid income. Very outgoing and assertive, socially perceptive and able to adapt her presentation, but notably low in cooperativeness—often blunt, judgmental, and hard to please, with a small social circle; she values honesty and loyalty and recognizes she “should” be kinder and a better listener. Highly analytical and enjoys complex thinking; strong logic/reasoning and numeracy, tends to deliberate and correct initial intuitions, and is generally realistic about her own performance. Extremely conscientious and structured, driven to optimize decisions and seek the “best” option, prefers clear answers and closure over ambiguity, and has a strong goal/loss-avoidance orientation; emotionally fairly steady with low anxiety and only mild depressive tendencies. Financially, she is risk-averse, impatient for delayed rewards, and strongly spendthrift/impulse-prone, yet uses mental “budgets” and categories; she has only modest general financial knowledge. Interpersonally she’s empathetic and can reciprocate fairness when trust is shown, but is wary of being taken advantage of, offers moderate fairness when bargaining, and is unwilling to give when sharing is purely voluntary; she also likes to feel distinctive and not just follow the crowd, with only moderate interest in minimalism and environmentalism.

Older (65+), married White male in the Northeast with a college education, high income, and full-time work; politically a conservative-leaning Democrat who attends religious services weekly. Socially confident and generally calm, he is personable and cooperative but strongly status/achievement-oriented, prioritizing personal success and providing for his family over warmth or emotional attunement. He tends to present himself in a favorable light and is skilled at adapting his behavior to social situations, while holding a somewhat flexible/uncertain self-concept. Decision-making is typically practical and “good-enough” rather than deeply analytical: he prefers simpler reasoning, relies on intuition, and may overestimate his own performance; he also shows strong present bias, making him prone to favor immediate benefits. Financially he is moderately risk-averse, uses mental “budgets,” and leans slightly spendthrift. Despite low empathic sensitivity, he will often act generously and trust others when it seems mutually beneficial or aligned with family values, and he has a moderately pro-environment orientation.

Older white male (65+), widowed and living alone in the Western US; college-educated, self-employed, middle income, weekly-attending Protestant, and very conservative Republican. He is highly curious and idea-driven—likes novelty, creativity, and complex thinking—and tends to be methodical, disciplined, and efficiency-focused, with a strong drive to optimize decisions rather than “good enough” choices. Socially he’s more reserved than outgoing, emotionally steady with low anxiety/depressive tendency, and has a clear, confident sense of who he is and a moderate desire for certainty. He values independence and personal achievement, prefers to do things his own way, and can be skeptical of strangers (low trust/reciprocity), yet in explicit fairness contexts he behaves very generously and wants to be seen as honest and fair. Interpersonally he’s not naturally empathic and knows it, relying more on listening and problem-solving than emotional attunement; he also tends to present himself in a socially acceptable light. Financially he is knowledgeable and somewhat tight with spending, moderately patient and risk-neutral, and not motivated by environmental concerns.

White, liberal Democratic atheist woman in her 30s–40s in the Western US; college-educated, high-income, self-employed, lives in a household of four, never married. Curious and creative with strong accumulated knowledge and excellent numeracy/financial literacy; can be reflective but generally prefers simple, “good-enough” decisions over exhaustive analysis. Emotionally intense and highly prone to anxiety/depressive feelings, with a strong desire to be self-sufficient and financially secure; often feels pressured to suppress emotions and caretake others. Socially perceptive and image-aware (good at adjusting to situations), moderately outgoing, and very empathetic, yet interpersonally tough-minded—values fairness and generosity but expects others may be greedy and manages a pull between self-interest and being unselfish. More self-advancing than relationship-maintenance oriented; comfortable with ambiguity and change, not minimalist, and tends to spend freely while being highly risk-averse and somewhat overconfident about her performance/standing.

Older (65+), married Black woman in the Northeast with postgraduate education and a high-income, full-time professional role (seasoned programmer aspiring to executive leadership). Highly conscientious, energetic, outgoing, and intellectually curious; enjoys complex problem-solving, learns quickly, and tends to be reflective and logic-oriented. Emotionally steady with very low anxiety, generally cooperative and empathic, and strongly pro-environment, but also ambitious and status-aware, wanting to be seen as competent, strategic, and distinctive. Socially savvy and image-conscious (high self-monitoring), using diplomacy and wit to navigate office politics while preferring direct, no-nonsense communication. Decision style is structured and goal-driven with moderate desire for closure and “good-enough” optimization, but can be impatient for immediate outcomes and prone to overestimating performance. Financially knowledgeable and numerate, comfortable with average risk, yet has a spendthrift streak. In fairness contexts she can be strategically generous when reciprocity is possible (trust/ultimatum) but markedly self-interested when unobserved and non-reciprocal (dictator), balancing self-benefit with not wanting to look greedy.

White Jewish (non-practicing) male in his 30s–40s living in the Northeast, cohabiting with a partner, full-time employed with high income and some college; politically independent/moderate. He is outgoing and assertive in many settings yet can feel socially insecure, but overall emotionally steady with low anxiety/depression. Highly conscientious and hard-working, comfortable with ambiguity, and tends to “satisfice” rather than over-optimize; enjoys thinking through complex problems and shows strong logical/numerical and financial reasoning. Values self-reliance and achievement more than harmony/communal warmth, with below-average empathy, and is candid rather than image-managing; he aspires to be dependable, confident, and less ego-driven. In choices, he’s relatively willing to take risks but strongly dislikes losses, can be impatient and present-focused, and prefers simplicity/minimalism; he’s moderately environmentally minded. In fairness contexts he’ll make reasonable splits when norms are clear, but he is notably distrustful of strangers and inclined to maximize his own payoff when trust or reciprocity is uncertain.

Young self-employed white male in the US South (college educated, mid-income), very liberal and nonreligious. Socially somewhat reserved but capable in groups; generally kind and fair-minded, willing to trust and share yet inclined to keep a slight edge for himself. Curious and open to new ideas with a noticeable desire to stand out and be influential, but less driven by relationship-maintenance than by personal skill and autonomy. Emotionally reactive and prone to worry, with a less stable self-concept and low self-monitoring, so he may be less strategic about impressions and can second-guess himself. Cognitively strong in verbal/deductive reasoning and practical knowledge (including finance) and tends to optimize decisions, but can be impatient in the moment and highly loss-averse—cautious about giving up what he has, reluctant to spend, and likely to overestimate his relative performance.

Married, high-income, college-educated White woman in the Western US (30–49), liberal/Democrat, culturally Catholic but rarely attends, working full-time in a larger household. Highly outgoing, organized, and ambitious yet strongly relationship- and community-oriented; tends to take charge as a “head of household”/leader and values being supportive and helpful. Curious and idea-open, enjoys thinking through complex topics, and prefers streamlined, minimalist choices with a notable environmental bent; also likes to stand out and optimize decisions rather than “good enough.” Generally calm under pressure but reports elevated anxiety/depressive symptoms and somewhat unclear self-concept, which can lead to rumination and second-guessing. In decisions, she is risk-averse and impatient with delayed rewards, financially and numerically capable, and prone to strong confidence in her judgments that may exceed actual performance. Socially, she is image-aware and tends to answer in socially desirable ways; she’s generous and cooperative when trust/reciprocity is salient, but can be tougher in one-sided situations and is unwilling to accept unfair deals.

Young Asian American woman in the Northeast, college-educated and self-employed, very liberal/Democrat and agnostic, living in a small household. She is emotionally sensitive and prone to anxiety and depressive rumination, with low self-confidence and unclear self-concept; she tends to overthink, anticipate disappointment, and hesitate to put herself out there, which can reduce follow-through and consistency despite good intentions. Socially she’s more reserved than outgoing, straightforward rather than image-managing, moderately cooperative, and notably empathetic and fairness-oriented—often prioritizing equitable splits, trust, and not being the first to violate goodwill, while still having some boundaries about what she will accept. Cognitively she is strong at logic, verbal reasoning, and numerical/financial thinking, generally accurate about her own abilities (not overconfident), and prefers structured, sensible decision rules; she’s moderately tolerant of risk, not especially impulsive, and sits near the tightwad side (spending can feel difficult). Values lean toward compassion, honesty, environmental concern, and practical minimalism, with relatively low desire to stand out; she aspires to become more confident, adaptable, independent, and reliably accountable.
